question: Which openly documented quadruped architecture should replace the Harness demo morphology as the starting point for a customizable MuJoCo-first robot?
missionAssumptions: The robot needs credible omnidirectional leg placement rather than four planar sticks.
The design must expose enough geometry, joint, actuator, and mass evidence to build an honest MuJoCo Assembly.
Fall recovery must be treated as an embodiment capability before Controller or RL optimization.
Deep customization is required, but source history and licenses must remain traceable.

inspection.method: Primary-source review plus shallow Git clones in a disposable directory outside the Mujica workspace.

sources.name: Open Dynamic Robot Initiative Solo12 hardware

license.evidence: Root LICENSE and README license section

inspectedAssets: 12-DoF Solo12 body and 3-DoF leg build documentation
electronics, wiring, calibration, bill of materials, range-of-motion, and inertia documentation
fit: Four 3-DoF legs provide hip abduction/adduction plus sagittal placement.
A modular torque-controlled actuator stack gives the morphology a real hardware basis.
Build and calibration evidence expose practical constraints that the current demo omits.
risks: The inspected hardware commit is from 2022 and upstream component availability must be refreshed.
The physical architecture is a reference baseline, not proof that all recovery poses are feasible.
Control, firmware, and master-board dependencies live in separate repositories and need their own ledger before reuse.

sources.name: ODRI robot_properties_solo

license.evidence: Root license.txt and README license section

inspectedAssets: joint naming for FL, FR, HL, and HR HAA/HFE/KFE joints
fit: Provides a traceable kinematic bridge from the open hardware to a simulation model.
Joint naming and resources can inform a clean MuJoCo reimplementation.
risks: It is not an MJCF source and should not be dropped into Mujica without an explicit conversion and validation step.
Model fidelity and inertial values still require comparison with the hardware documentation.

sources.name: MuJoCo Menagerie Unitree Go2

license.evidence: unitree_go2/LICENSE; the Menagerie root explicitly requires per-model license review

inspectedAssets: documented URDF-to-MJCF conversion and contact edits
fit: Strong reference for readable, production-shaped MuJoCo modeling and contact setup.
Useful visual and structural comparison for a 12-DoF commercial morphology.
risks: A licensed MJCF model does not establish open manufacturing CAD, electronics, or hardware rights.
It should calibrate modeling quality, not become the claimed open hardware architecture.

sources.name: mjbots quad

license.evidence: Root LICENSE and per-file headers; README says most files are Apache-2.0

openness.cad: 3MF parts plus externally linked Fusion 360 assembly

inspectedAssets: walking robot control and inverse kinematics
assembly, operation, maintenance, and calibration documentation
fit: Best inspected example of one repository joining a physical robot, simulator, controller, maintenance, and human interface.
Useful reference for Mujica's hardware-to-Studio lifecycle.
risks: The phrase 'most files' requires path-by-path license verification before copying.
The overall editable CAD assembly is externally hosted and was not established as a repository-owned source asset.

sources.name: Stanford Doggo

license.evidence: Root LICENSE covers repository content; linked Fusion 360 CAD and code submodules require separate boundary checks

inspectedAssets: linked CAD plus Doggo and ODrive submodule identities
fit: Useful reference for high-power, backdrivable leg transmission and explicit actuator tradeoffs.
Demonstrates dynamic jumping and backflip performance from a reproducible research platform.
risks: Planar 2-DoF legs constrain lateral placement and are a poor default for the current omnidirectional mission.
The repository is end-of-life and important assets sit behind external CAD or separate submodules.

sources.name: Stanford Pupper v1
inspectedAssets: gait, stance, swing, inverse-kinematics, IMU, joystick, and hardware interfaces
fit: Readable educational decomposition for a cheap deterministic Controller probe.
Useful example of separating gait scheduling, stance, swing, IK, and hardware interfaces.
risks: The inspected repository does not contain the manufacturing design needed for a new physical baseline.

rationale: Solo12 is the only inspected candidate that joins a genuinely open 12-DoF physical architecture with build, actuator, electronics, calibration, range-of-motion, inertia, URDF, and mesh evidence.
Three joints per leg directly address the current demo's missing lateral authority without adding an unproven waist as the first reaction.
Adapting the architecture into a new Mujica Assembly keeps deep customization possible while avoiding an unnecessary fork of unrelated upstream software stacks.
Go2 supplies a current MuJoCo model-quality reference without being misrepresented as open hardware.
notAuthorizedYet: No upstream source or binary asset may be copied into Mujica until a path-level attribution record is added.
No GitHub fork is created by this study.
No self-righting capability is inferred from range-of-motion documentation alone.
No Controller or RL budget resumes until the adapted design passes static reach/contact probes and a human visual review.

nextDesignBrief.name: Solo12-informed Mujica quadruped baseline
requirements: Implement a clean, parameterized 12-DoF Assembly with HAA, HFE, and KFE joints per leg.
Source dimensions, mass, inertia, joint ranges, and actuator limits from traceable upstream facts or mark them as explicit hypotheses.
Model torso, hip packaging, feet, collision geometry, and cable/joint limits rather than copying the current block body.
Generate local design previews for standing, folded, supine, prone, and lateral recovery poses.
Compare the adaptation against the current demo fixture using identical static reach/contact probes before any dynamic optimization.
Ask a human to review the candidate form and force paths before declaring it the project baseline.
nextDesignBrief.exitCondition: A checked-in Design Study shows a physically plausible 12-DoF baseline with authoritative collision-free standing and recovery contact opportunities, and human review accepts its overall form for bounded dynamic probes.
